description: cmd_log_tip calls percent_encode(group) to build the query string. percent_encode's unreserved set is ALPHA / DIGIT / - _ . ~ + . It does not encode '#' (fragment delimiter) or '?' (query delimiter). A group name containing '#' would be interpreted by the HTTP layer as a fragment, truncating the query. A group name with '?' would split the query string. Real Usenet group names (RFC 3977) cannot contain these characters, but a future extension or operator error could pass such a string. The comment about '+' being preserved for newsgroup names is correct, but '#' and '?' should also be documented as safe-to-exclude (because they cannot appear in valid group names) rather than silently relying on this invariant.
title: ctl: percent_encode does not encode '#' or '?' characters in group names
